stemMd: Fungi were once classified as plants. Which statement correctly describes a difference between the two kingdoms?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Fungi are heterotrophs with cell walls made of chitin, not cellulose

options.label: B
options.textMd: Fungal cells have no cell wall, whereas plant cells have one

options.label: C
options.textMd: Fungi store carbohydrate mainly as starch, whereas plants store it as glycogen

options.label: D
options.textMd: Fungi are prokaryotes, whereas plants are eukaryotes

options.label: E
options.textMd: Fungi carry out photosynthesis using a pigment other than chlorophyll

explanationMd:
Compare the two kingdoms feature by feature.

| Feature | Plants | Fungi |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cell type | eukaryotic | eukaryotic |
| Nutrition | autotrophic (photosynthesis) | heterotrophic, by absorption |
| Cell wall | cellulose | chitin |
| Carbohydrate store | starch | glycogen |

Fungi secrete enzymes into their surroundings and absorb the products, as moulds do on bread; they cannot photosynthesise. Their walls are made of **chitin**, the same polysaccharide found in insect exoskeletons.

**Check:** only one statement matches the table; each of the others gets a row wrong, or swaps the two kingdoms.

distractorRationale.d: Both fungi and plants are eukaryotes, with a nucleus and membrane-bound organelles. Prokaryotes are bacteria and archaea.
distractorRationale.e: Fungi have no photosynthetic pigment at all; they are heterotrophs that feed on organic matter made by other organisms.
distractorRationale.b: Fungal cells do have a cell wall; it is made of chitin instead of the cellulose found in plants.
distractorRationale.c: This swaps the two storage molecules: plants store starch, while fungi, like animals, store glycogen.

accessibilityText: A short text question with no figure. Fungi were once classified as plants, and the question asks which statement correctly describes a difference between the two kingdoms. The choices are: fungi are heterotrophs with cell walls made of chitin, not cellulose; fungal cells have no cell wall whereas plant cells have one; fungi store carbohydrate mainly as starch whereas plants store glycogen; fungi are prokaryotes whereas plants are eukaryotes; fungi photosynthesise using a pigment other than chlorophyll. The explanation contains a table comparing plants and fungi by cell type, nutrition, cell wall and carbohydrate store.

provenance.notes: Original item. Tests the defining features of the kingdom Fungi against plants.

review.author: tolc-f-wave8-biochem-author

independentSolve.workingNotes: Fungi are heterotrophic eukaryotes with chitin cell walls, unlike autotrophic plants with cellulose walls. Fungi do have walls, are eukaryotes, do not photosynthesise, and store glycogen (plants store starch), so the reversed storage statement is false. [A second, separate blind solve (blind-reviewer-wave8-tolcf-biochem-run1) reached the same answer: Fungi are heterotrophic eukaryotes with chitin cell walls, while plants have cellulose walls and photosynthesise. The other options are wrong: fungi do have walls, fungi store glycogen and plants store starch (reversed), fungi are eukaryotes, and fungi do not photosynthesise.]
